correctness.rationale: For every m>=1 the displayed necessary-and-sufficient 0^x 1 0^(m-1-x) root inequalities are established in both directions; all possible roots form an interval. Exact interval-count convolution and finite differences prove the multiplicity formula and generating series for arbitrary m and t. The total count agrees with the established 2023 count; an independent interleaving DP checks all 9500 two-one words and 175100 candidate roots at m<=24, plus 100 algebraic lengths. The weak limit follows from exact coefficients and Riemann summation. No finite check is misrepresented as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Multiplicity of distinct roots measures the natural ambiguity of a self-shuffle, directly motivated by the 2025 roots paper. The result provides an all-length exact classification and rational two-parameter generating function for the first nonconstant fixed-content layer, plus the nondegenerate mixed atomic/triangular scaling law and sharp root support; these are substantive beyond the already known existence and total counts.
